content: 1. A systematic review has been conducted to identify symptoms and concerns among children and young people with life-limiting and life-threatening conditions, emphasizing meaningful health outcomes. This review was published in Patient in 2019. 2. A study reviewed whether clinical management guidelines for COVID-19 in African countries align with African quality palliative care standards. This analysis of current guidelines was published in Journal of Pain and Symptom Management in 2021. 3. Research has highlighted the chronic comorbidities present in children and adolescents with perinatally acquired HIV in sub-Saharan Africa during the era of antiretroviral therapy. This study was published in The Lancet Child & Adolescent Health in 2020. 4. Projections of the global burden of serious health-related suffering by 2060, categorized by world regions, age groups, and health conditions, were published in The Lancet Global Health in 2019. 5. A modeling study explored future challenges in the clinical care of an aging population living with HIV, published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2015. 6. An analysis of mortality and causes of death among people diagnosed with HIV in the era of highly active antiretroviral therapy, compared to the general population, was published in The Lancet Public Health in 2017. 7. A study determined standardized causes of death among infants, children, and adolescents living with HIV in Asia, published in AIDS in 2020. 8. The World Health Organization (WHO) has emphasized the importance of integrating palliative care into comprehensive care throughout the life course, as outlined in their guidelines accessed in June 2021. 9. Public preferences and priorities for end-of-life care in Kenya were assessed through a population-based street survey, published in BMC Palliative Care in 2014. 10. A similar study on public priorities for end-of-life care in Namibia was published in Journal of Pain and Symptom Management in 2014. 11. Preferences for the place of death among individuals with advanced cancer were surveyed across multiple European countries, with findings published in Annals of Oncology in 2012. 12. A population-level comparison of the place of death for people with HIV across 11 countries was conducted using death certificate data, published in BMC Infectious Diseases in 2018. 13. A systematic review examined the needs, experiences, and preferences of sexual minorities for end-of-life and palliative care, published in Journal of Palliative Medicine in 2012. 14. Recommendations to reduce inequalities for LGBT individuals facing advanced illness were developed through a national qualitative interview study, published in Palliative Medicine in 2018. 15. A systematic review synthesized the bereavement experiences of lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender individuals who have lost a partner, published in Palliative Medicine in 2016. 16. A qualitative study explored barriers to accessing palliative care for key populations, including LGBT individuals and sex workers, in Zimbabwe, published in BMJ Global Health in 2017. 17. A multi-country qualitative study identified self-reported symptoms, concerns, and priority outcomes among children with life-limiting illnesses, aiming to improve person-centered quality care. This was published in Palliative Medicine in 2020. 18. A systematic review evaluated whether palliative care improves outcomes for patients with HIV/AIDS, published in Sexually Transmitted Infections in 2005. 19. A randomized controlled trial in Kenya analyzed the active components of a person-centered intervention for individuals on HIV treatment, published in BMC Infectious Diseases in 2018. 20. A nurse-led palliative care intervention for HIV-positive patients on antiretroviral therapy in Kenya demonstrated significant outcomes, published in The Lancet HIV in 2015. 21. A systematic review assessed the cost-effectiveness of palliative care in lowand middle-income countries, published in BMJ Supportive & Palliative Care in 2019. 22. A hospital-based palliative care service for patients with advanced organ failure in sub-Saharan Africa was shown to reduce hospital admissions and increase home death rates, published in Journal of Pain and Symptom Management in 2014. 23. The WHO has developed guidelines to integrate palliative care and symptom relief into primary health care, emphasizing the importance of planners, implementers, and managers in this process. 24. A study evaluated the impact of age at antiretroviral therapy initiation on growth recovery in HIV-infected children in West Africa, published in Pediatric Infectious Disease Journal in 2015. 25. Research has shown that older age at the initiation of antiretroviral therapy predicts lower bone mineral density in children with perinatally acquired HIV in Zimbabwe, published in Bone in 2019. 26. 27. A study identified adolescent age as an independent risk factor for abnormal spirometry among people living with HIV in Kenya, published in AIDS in 2018. 28. The Global Lung Initiative 2012 reference values for spirometry were evaluated for African children, published in American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine in 2017. 29. A study examined lung function in South African adolescents with perinatally acquired HIV treated with long-term antiretroviral therapy, published in Annals of the American Thoracic Society in 2017. 30. Neurologic disease in HIV-infected children and the impact of combination antiretroviral therapy were reviewed, published in Reviews in Medical Virology in 2014. 31. A study validated the Youth International HIV Dementia Scale for screening HIV-associated neurocognitive disorders in perinatally infected adolescents, published in AIDS in 2019. 32. Emotional and behavioral disorders among perinatally HIV-infected youth in Uganda were analyzed in the CHAKA study, published in Social Psychiatry and Psychiatric Epidemiology in 2019. 33. Mental health and functional competence in the Cape Town Adolescent Antiretroviral Cohort were studied, published in Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2019. 34. A systematic review examined HIV-associated malignancies in children, published in Current Opinion in HIV and AIDS in 2017. 35. The incidence of AIDS-defining and other cancers in HIV-positive children in South Africa was analyzed through a record linkage study, published in Pediatric Infectious Disease Journal in 2016. 36. Patterns of HIV, tuberculosis, and non-communicable disease multimorbidity in peri-urban South Africa were studied, published in BMC Infectious Diseases in 2015. 37. 38. The WHO promotes a public health approach to antiretroviral therapy (ART), emphasizing simplified and standardized ART delivery to support decentralization, task sharing, and community-based care. 39. Despite progress in ART access, challenges remain, including disengagement from care after treatment initiation, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa, where one-third of adults disengage within five years. 40. WHO guidelines emphasize people-centered care, rapid ART initiation, and addressing structural barriers such as stigma, discrimination, and violence, particularly for vulnerable populations.
